programme: GLIS3, THRA, USF2 and AEBP1 form an insulin/thyroid-hormone-responsive metabolic transcription module: GLIS3 sits directly on the insulin gene program (INS, NEUROG3, PAX6) and is the same factor whose loss causes neonatal diabetes with congenital hypothyroidism; THRA is the thyroid hormone receptor executing T3-dependent transcription on glucose- and lipid-handling genes (SLC2A4/GLUT4, UCP3, ABCA1) and on pituitary feedback genes (GH1, TSHB); USF2 regulates the same cholesterol/lipid and glucose-metabolic gene class (ABCA1, ACACA, PKLR, GCGR, DPP4); AEBP1 sits downstream in lipid-handling, APOE/CD36/FABP4-driven microglial and astrocyte programs. Together they describe a peripheral insulin-lipid-thyroid transcriptional axis rather than a physical complex.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's Disease this axis maps onto the recognized insulin-resistance/lipid-handling comorbidity: GLIS3 sits in the same T2D-GWAS pathway shown to modify AD risk (PMID 26499758) and scores at the 97th percentile for AD association; AEBP1 marks disease-associated microglia/astrocytes and is transcriptionally dysregulated in late-onset AD cortex, acting on APOE/CD36/FABP4 lipid-uptake genes (PMID 41516171, 38568322, 38345650); THRA's targets (SLC2A4, ABCA1, UCP3) place thyroid-hormone-driven glucose/cholesterol handling in hippocampal pathway analysis (PMID 41317176).
role_in_b: In Fibromyalgia the only direct evidence is for THRA: adults with resistance to thyroid hormone (a THRA-centered phenotype) present with the fatigue, diffuse myalgia and cognitive complaints that overlap fibromyalgia's clinical picture (PMID 37469961), consistent with fibromyalgia's separately reported associations with subclinical hypothyroidism and metabolic-syndrome-like states. GLIS3, USF2 and AEBP1 have no fibromyalgia-specific evidence in this record; their role there is inferred from the same target genes, not shown.
shared_axis: Both conditions are separately linked in the clinical literature to disturbed insulin/glucose and thyroid-hormone signaling (AD via the insulin-resistance/'type 3 diabetes' axis, fibromyalgia via thyroid-hormone-resistance-like symptom overlap). A shared peripheral (blood) metabolic-endocrine transcriptional signature — insulin/glucose genes (GLIS3, USF2), lipid/cholesterol genes (USF2, AEBP1) and thyroid-hormone target genes (THRA) — could reflect a common systemic dysregulation state that manifests as amyloid/microglial burden in brain and as diffuse pain/fatigue in muscle, without either disease directly causing the other.
reasoning: The module is nameable from real gene identities (INS, ABCA1, SLC2A4, CD36, FABP4, GH1/TSHB) and several factors are independently placed in AD by more than one retrieved paper, so this is not a bare co-occurrence. But no retrieved source studies AD and fibromyalgia together through this axis — the fibromyalgia side rests on a single THRA paper plus inference from shared target genes, and USF2 has no disease-specific citation at all — so the cross-disease claim is reasoning, not retrieval.
support: PMID 26499758 - directly ties T2D/insulin GWAS loci (GLIS3's pathway) to AD risk; PMID 37085326 - GLIS3-linked variation associates with amyloid/cognition/MRI in AD; PMID 41516171 - AEBP1 drives microglial lipid-handling phenotype shift in AD; PMID 38568322 - AEBP1 transcriptionally dysregulated in late-onset AD cortex; PMID 38345650 - AEBP1 marks disease-associated astrocytes in AD; PMID 41317176 - THRA pathway analysis in AD hippocampus; PMID 37469961 - THRA/thyroid-hormone-resistance clinical phenotype overlapping fibromyalgia symptoms.
how_to_falsify: In matched blood samples from AD and fibromyalgia patient groups, test whether expression of the shared targets (INS, ABCA1, SLC2A4, CD36, FABP4) tracks with independently measured insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and thyroid status (free T3/T4, TSH). If target-gene concordance between the two diseases persists in patients with normal insulin and thyroid biochemistry, the proposed metabolic-endocrine axis is not the explanation for the shared factor signature.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|brain and only 3 independent cohort pairs underlie the 32 patient-group comparisons, so apparent concordance could partly reflect shared cohort/batch structure rather than 32 independent replications. Fibromyalgia has essentially no direct Open Targets or literature support for any of these factors except the one THRA paper, so that half of the story is inferred from AD-side and target-gene evidence, not observed. The single-subgroup exclusions (CREBBP, RFX3, RELB, OTX1, KLF16, FOXO4) rule out this being an artifact of one patient group, and the tissue-generic exclusions (RELB, E2F2/3, NR4A3, ERG, FOXO4, STAT1/3, IRF8, GFI1, PRDM1, ELK3) confirm the retained signal is not just generic hematopoietic/immune background — but AIP was deliberately left out of the programme because its 'AD' citation (D-AIP, an amyloid-interacting peptide) is a name collision with the AIP gene, not real evidence for the transcription factor.
